method: Wrote a from-scratch script (/tmp/independent_critpath.py, not imported into the repo and NOT importing command-center/p2-wave/probes/CC-0016/phase_graph_gate.py or any of its functions) that: (1) loads command-center/PHASE-GRAPH.json directly via json.load, (2) filters edges[] to type==HARD (32 of 46), (3) builds its own adjacency list and runs a from-scratch Kahn's-algorithm topological sort as an independent acyclicity check (all 21 nodes drained -> acyclic), (4) runs its own longest-path-by-node-count DP over the topological order (dist[n]=1+max(dist[pred]) for pred in HARD-predecessors), (5) reconstructs the path via predecessor pointers. Independently cross-checked with a SECOND, structurally different method: unrestricted DFS enumeration of every maximal simple path over the same HARD-only adjacency (brute force, no DP, no topological order dependency), collecting all paths tied at the observed maximum length. Both methods agree exactly. Also independently verified: every consecutive step of the recorded critical_path.path is present in edges[] with type==HARD (not assumed); the recorded critical_path.hard_edge_count (10) equals len(path)-1; and the top-level edge_count/hard_edge_count/soft_edge_count fields (46/32/14) match direct recomputation from edges[].
